verses.1MA 6:12: But now I remember the evils which I did at Jerusalem, and that I took all the vessels of silver and gold that were in it, and sent out to destroy the inhabitants of Judah without a cause.
verses.1MA 6:13: I perceive that it is because of this that these evils have come upon me. Behold, I am perishing through great grief in a strange land.”
verses.1PE 1:10: Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently. They prophesied of the grace that would come to you,
verses.1PE 1:11: searching for who or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them pointed to when he predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow them.
verses.1PE 1:12: To them it was revealed that they served not themselves, but you, in these things, which now have been announced to you through those who preached the Good News to you by the Holy Spirit sent out from heaven; which things angels desire to look into.
verses.1PE 1:13: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
verses.1PE 1:14: as children of obedience, not conforming yourselves according to your former lusts as in your ignorance,
verses.1PE 1:15: but just as he who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior,
verses.1PE 1:16: because it is written, “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
verses.1PE 1:17: If you call on him as Father, who without respect of persons judges according to each man’s work, pass the time of your living as foreigners here in reverent fear,
verses.1PE 1:18: knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things like silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers,
verses.1PE 1:19: but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ,
verses.1PE 1:20: who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in this last age for your sake,
verses.1PE 1:21: who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.
verses.1PE 1:22: Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently,
verses.1PE 1:23: having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and remains forever.
verses.1PE 1:24: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls;
verses.1PE 1:25: but the Lord’s word endures forever.” This is the word of Good News which was preached to you.
verses.1PE 1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
verses.1PE 1:4: to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
verses.1PE 1:5: who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
verses.1PE 1:6: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
verses.1PE 1:7: that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes, even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
verses.1PE 1:8: whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
verses.1PE 1:9: receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
verses.1PE 2:2: as newborn babies, long for the pure spiritual milk, that with it you may grow,
verses.1PE 2:3: if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is gracious.
verses.1PE 2:4: Come to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.
verses.1PE 2:5: You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
verses.1PE 2:9: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, that you may proclaim the excellence of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
verses.1PE 2:10: In the past, you were not a people, but now are God’s people, who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
verses.1PE 2:11: Beloved, I beg you as foreigners and pilgrims to abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul,
verses.1PE 2:12: having good behavior among the nations, so in that of which they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good works and glorify God in the day of visitation.
verses.1PE 2:20: For what glory is it if, when you sin, you patiently endure beating? But if when you do well, you patiently endure suffering, this is commendable with God.
verses.1PE 2:21: For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps,
verses.1PE 2:22: who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.”
verses.1PE 2:23: When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.
verses.1PE 2:24: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
verses.1PE 2:25: For you were going astray like sheep; but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
verses.1PE 2:6: Because it is contained in Scripture, “Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious. He who believes in him will not be disappointed.”
verses.1PE 2:7: For you who believe therefore is the honor, but for those who are disobedient, “The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone,”
verses.1PE 2:8: and, “a stumbling stone and a rock of offense.” For they stumble at the word, being disobedient, to which also they were appointed.
verses.1PE 3:1: In the same way, wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, so that, even if any don’t obey the Word, they may be won by the behavior of their wives without a word,
verses.1PE 3:2: seeing your pure behavior in fear.
verses.1PE 3:3: Let your beauty come not from the outward adorning of braiding your hair, and of wearing gold ornaments or of putting on fine clothing,
verses.1PE 3:4: but from the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptible adornment of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious in God’s sight.
verses.1PE 3:5: For this is how in the past the holy women who hoped in God also adorned themselves, being in subjection to their own husbands.
verses.1PE 3:6: So Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, whose children you now are if you do well and are not put in fear by any terror.
verses.1PE 3:7: You husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, giving honor to the woman as to the weaker vessel, as also being joint heirs of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.
verses.1PE 3:8: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, courteous,
verses.1PE 3:9: not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.
verses.1PE 3:14: But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t fear what they fear, neither be troubled.”
verses.1PE 3:15: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
verses.1PE 3:16: having a good conscience. Thus, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disappointed who curse your good way of life in Christ.
verses.1PE 3:17: For it is better, if it is God’s will, that you suffer for doing what is right than for doing evil.
verses.1PE 3:18: Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit,
verses.1PE 3:19: in whom he also went and preached to the spirits in prison,
verses.1PE 3:20: who before were disobedient when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ship was being built. In it, few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.
verses.1PE 3:21: This is a symbol of baptism, which now saves you—not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
verses.1PE 3:22: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers being made subject to him.
verses.1PE 4:12: Beloved, don’t be astonished at the fiery trial which has come upon you to test you, as though a strange thing happened to you.
verses.1PE 4:13: But because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, that at the revelation of his glory you also may rejoice with exceeding joy.
verses.1PE 4:14: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you. On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.
verses.1PE 4:15: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evil doer, or a meddler in other men’s matters.
verses.1PE 4:16: But if one of you suffers for being a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God in this matter.
verses.1PE 4:17: For the time has come for judgment to begin with the household of God. If it begins first with us, what will happen to those who don’t obey the Good News of God?
verses.1PE 4:18: “If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?”
verses.1PE 4:19: Therefore let them also who suffer according to the will of God in doing good entrust their souls to him, as to a faithful Creator.
verses.1PE 4:7: But the end of all things is near. Therefore be of sound mind, self-controlled, and sober in prayer.
verses.1PE 4:8: And above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.
verses.1PE 4:9: Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
verses.1PE 4:10: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.
verses.1PE 4:11: If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1PE 5:1: Therefore I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and who will also share in the glory that will be revealed:
verses.1PE 5:2: shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly;
verses.1PE 5:3: not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.
verses.1PE 5:4: When the chief Shepherd is revealed, you will receive the crown of glory that doesn’t fade away.
verses.1PE 5:5: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
verses.1PE 5:6: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
verses.1PE 5:7: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
verses.1PE 5:8: Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
verses.1PE 5:9: Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
verses.1PE 5:10: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
verses.1PE 5:11: To him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1PE 5:12: Through Silvanus, our faithful brother, as I consider him, I have written to you briefly, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which you stand.
verses.1PE 5:13: She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you. So does Mark, my son.
verses.1PE 5:14: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
verses.1SA 15:16: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Stay, and I will tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” He said to him, “Say on.”
verses.1SA 15:17: Samuel said, “Though you were little in your own sight, weren’t you made the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel;
verses.1SA 15:18: and the LORD sent you on a journey, and said, ‘Go, and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.’
verses.1SA 15:19: Why then didn’t you obey the LORD’s voice, but took the plunder, and did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight?”
verses.1SA 15:20: Saul said to Samuel, “But I have obeyed the LORD’s voice, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
verses.1SA 15:21: But the people took of the plunder, sheep and cattle, the best of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal.”
verses.1SA 15:22: Samuel said, “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the LORD’s voice? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.
verses.1SA 15:23: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because you have rejected the LORD’s word, he has also rejected you from being king.”
verses.1SA 16:1: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided a king for myself among his sons.”
verses.1SA 16:2: Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me.” The LORD said, “Take a heifer with you, and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’
verses.1SA 16:3: Call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you shall do. You shall anoint to me him whom I name to you.”
verses.1SA 16:4: Samuel did that which the LORD spoke, and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came to meet him trembling, and said, “Do you come peaceably?”
verses.1SA 16:5: He said, “Peaceably; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice.” He sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
verses.1SA 16:6: When they had come, he looked at Eliab, and said, “Surely the LORD’s anointed is before him.”
verses.1SA 16:7: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
verses.1SA 16:8: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. He said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”
verses.1SA 16:9: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. He said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”
verses.1SA 16:10: Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen these.”
verses.1SA 16:11: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are all your children here?” He said, “There remains yet the youngest. Behold, he is keeping the sheep.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and get him, for we will not sit down until he comes here.”
verses.1SA 16:12: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. The LORD said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”
verses.1SA 16:13: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the middle of his brothers. Then the LORD’s Spirit came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up and went to Ramah.
verses.1SA 17:32: David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.”
verses.1SA 17:33: Saul said to David, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for you are but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.”
verses.1SA 17:37: David said, “The LORD, who delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.” Saul said to David, “Go! The LORD will be with you.”
verses.1SA 17:40: He took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag which he had. His sling was in his hand; and he came near to the Philistine.
verses.1SA 17:41: The Philistine walked and came near to David; and the man who bore the shield went before him.
verses.1SA 17:42: When the Philistine looked around and saw David, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and had a good looking face.
verses.1SA 17:43: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” The Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.1SA 17:44: The Philistine said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and to the animals of the field.”
verses.1SA 17:45: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
verses.1SA 17:46: Today, the LORD will deliver you into my hand. I will strike you and take your head from off you. I will give the dead bodies of the army of the Philistines today to the birds of the sky and to the wild animals of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,
verses.1SA 17:47: and that all this assembly may know that the LORD doesn’t save with sword and spear; for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
verses.1SA 17:48: When the Philistine arose, and walked and came near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
verses.1SA 17:49: David put his hand in his bag, took a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth.
verses.1SA 17:50: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him; but there was no sword in David’s hand.
verses.1SA 18:6: As they came, when David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet King Saul with tambourines, with joy, and with instruments of music.
verses.1SA 18:7: The women sang to one another as they played, and said, “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.”
verses.1SA 18:8: Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him. He said, “They have credited David with ten thousands, and they have only credited me with thousands. What can he have more but the kingdom?”
verses.1SA 18:9: Saul watched David from that day and forward.
verses.1SA 19:1: Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan, Saul’s son, greatly delighted in David.
verses.1SA 19:2: Jonathan told David, saying, “Saul my father seeks to kill you. Now therefore, please take care of yourself in the morning, live in a secret place, and hide yourself.
verses.1SA 19:3: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will talk with my father about you; and if I see anything, I will tell you.”
verses.1SA 19:4: Jonathan spoke good of David to Saul his father, and said to him, “Don’t let the king sin against his servant, against David; because he has not sinned against you, and because his works have been very good toward you;
verses.1SA 19:5: for he put his life in his hand and struck the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great victory for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood, to kill David without a cause?”
verses.1SA 19:6: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan; and Saul swore, “As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death.”
verses.1SA 19:7: Jonathan called David, and Jonathan showed him all those things. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as before.
verses.1SA 1:1: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
verses.1SA 1:2: He had two wives. The name of one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
verses.1SA 1:3: This man went up out of his city from year to year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of Armies in Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests to the LORD, were there.
verses.1SA 1:4: When the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters;
verses.1SA 1:5: but he gave a double portion to Hannah, for he loved Hannah, but the LORD had shut up her womb.
verses.1SA 1:6: Her rival provoked her severely, to irritate her, because the LORD had shut up her womb.
verses.1SA 1:7: So year by year, when she went up to the LORD’s house, her rival provoked her. Therefore she wept, and didn’t eat.
verses.1SA 1:8: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Hannah, why do you weep? Why don’t you eat? Why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
verses.1SA 1:20: When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked him of the LORD.”
verses.1SA 1:21: The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.
verses.1SA 1:22: But Hannah didn’t go up, for she said to her husband, “Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD, and stay there forever.”
verses.1SA 1:24: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah of meal, and a container of wine, and brought him to the LORD’s house in Shiloh. The child was young.
verses.1SA 1:25: They killed the bull, and brought the child to Eli.
verses.1SA 1:26: She said, “Oh, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to the LORD.
verses.1SA 1:27: I prayed for this child, and the LORD has given me my petition which I asked of him.
verses.1SA 1:28: Therefore I have also given him to the LORD. As long as he lives he is given to the LORD.” He worshiped the LORD there.
verses.1SA 1:9: So Hannah rose up after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the LORD’s temple.
verses.1SA 1:10: She was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly.
verses.1SA 1:11: She vowed a vow, and said, “LORD of Armies, if you will indeed look at the affliction of your servant and remember me, and not forget your servant, but will give to your servant a boy, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
verses.1SA 1:12: As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli saw her mouth.
verses.1SA 1:13: Now Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.
verses.1SA 1:14: Eli said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Get rid of your wine!”
verses.1SA 1:15: Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before the LORD.
verses.1SA 1:16: Don’t consider your servant a wicked woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”
verses.1SA 1:17: Then Eli answered, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”
verses.1SA 1:18: She said, “Let your servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman went her way and ate; and her facial expression wasn’t sad any more.
verses.1SA 1:19: They rose up in the morning early and worshiped the LORD, then returned and came to their house to Ramah. Then Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.
verses.1SA 24:2: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men on the rocks of the wild goats.
verses.1SA 24:3: He came to the sheep pens by the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to relieve himself. Now David and his men were staying in the innermost parts of the cave.
verses.1SA 24:4: David’s men said to him, “Behold, the day of which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem good to you.’” Then David arose and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe secretly.
verses.1SA 24:5: Afterward, David’s heart struck him because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
verses.1SA 24:6: He said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
verses.1SA 24:7: So David checked his men with these words, and didn’t allow them to rise against Saul. Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
verses.1SA 24:8: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave and cried after Saul, saying, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the earth, and showed respect.
verses.1SA 24:9: David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to men’s words, saying, ‘Behold, David seeks to harm you’?
verses.1SA 24:10: Behold, today your eyes have seen how the LORD had delivered you today into my hand in the cave. Some urged me to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ‘I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD’s anointed.’
verses.1SA 24:11: Moreover, my father, behold, yes, see the skirt of your robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe and didn’t kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor disobedience in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my life to take it.
verses.1SA 24:12: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me of you; but my hand will not be on you.
verses.1SA 24:13: As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Out of the wicked comes wickedness;’ but my hand will not be on you.
verses.1SA 24:14: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
verses.1SA 24:15: May the LORD therefore be judge, and give sentence between me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of your hand.”
verses.1SA 24:16: It came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, “Is that your voice, my son David?” Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.1SA 24:17: He said to David, “You are more righteous than I; for you have done good to me, whereas I have done evil to you.
verses.1SA 24:18: You have declared today how you have dealt well with me, because when the LORD had delivered me up into your hand, you didn’t kill me.
verses.1SA 24:19: For if a man finds his enemy, will he let him go away unharmed? Therefore may the LORD reward you good for that which you have done to me today.
verses.1SA 24:20: Now, behold, I know that you will surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.
verses.1SA 26:2: Then Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.1SA 26:7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night; and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the place of the wagons, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay around him.

verses.1SA 4:3: When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let’s get the ark of the LORD’s covenant out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”
verses.1SA 4:4: So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Armies, who sits above the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

verses.1SA 4:6: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” They understood that the LORD’s ark had come into the camp.
verses.1SA 4:7: The Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come into the camp.” They said, “Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.
verses.1SA 4:8: Woe to us! Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
verses.1SA 4:9: Be strong and behave like men, O you Philistines, that you not be servants to the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like men, and fight!”
verses.1SA 4:10: The Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. There was a very great slaughter; for thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.

verses.1SA 8:11: He said, “This will be the way of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them as his servants, for his chariots and to be his horsemen; and they will run before his chariots.

verses.1SA 8:13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers, to be cooks, and to be bakers.
verses.1SA 8:14: He will take your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, even your best, and give them to his servants.

verses.1SA 8:16: He will take your male servants, your female servants, your best young men, and your donkeys, and assign them to his own work.

verses.1TH 1:1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1TH 1:2: We always give thanks to God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers,
verses.1TH 1:3: remembering without ceasing your work of faith and labor of love and perseverance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father.
verses.1TH 1:4: We know, brothers loved by God, that you are chosen,

verses.1TH 1:8: For from you the word of the Lord has been declared, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith toward God has gone out, so that we need not say anything.
verses.1TH 1:9: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of a reception we had from you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God,
verses.1TH 1:10: and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead: Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath to come.
verses.1TH 1:6: You became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit,

verses.1TH 2:1: For you yourselves know, brothers, our visit to you wasn’t in vain,
verses.1TH 2:2: but having suffered before and been shamefully treated, as you know, at Philippi, we grew bold in our God to tell you the Good News of God in much conflict.
verses.1TH 2:3: For our exhortation is not of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deception.
verses.1TH 2:4: But even as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the Good News, so we speak—not as pleasing men, but God, who tests our hearts.
verses.1TH 2:5: For neither were we at any time found using words of flattery, as you know, nor a cloak of covetousness (God is witness),
verses.1TH 2:6: nor seeking glory from men (neither from you nor from others), when we might have claimed authority as apostles of Christ.
verses.1TH 2:7: But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
verses.1TH 2:8: Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.
verses.1TH 2:13: For this cause we also thank God without ceasing that when you received from us the word of the message of God, you accepted it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, God’s word, which also works in you who believe.
verses.1TH 2:9: For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail; for working night and day, that we might not burden any of you, we preached to you the Good News of God.
verses.1TH 2:10: You are witnesses with God how holy, righteously, and blamelessly we behaved ourselves toward you who believe.
verses.1TH 2:11: As you know, we exhorted, comforted, and implored every one of you, as a father does his own children,
verses.1TH 2:12: to the end that you should walk worthily of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.

verses.1TI 3:1: This is a faithful saying: someone who seeks to be an overseer desires a good work.
verses.1TI 3:2: The overseer therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable, good at teaching;
verses.1TI 3:3: not a drinker, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous;
verses.1TI 3:4: one who rules his own house well, having children in subjection with all reverence;

verses.1TI 3:6: not a new convert, lest being puffed up he fall into the same condemnation as the devil.
verses.1TI 3:7: Moreover he must have good testimony from those who are outside, to avoid falling into reproach and the snare of the devil.
verses.1TI 3:8: Servants, in the same way, must be reverent, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not greedy for money,
verses.1TI 3:9: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
verses.1TI 3:10: Let them also first be tested; then let them serve if they are blameless.
verses.1TI 3:11: Their wives in the same way must be reverent, not slanderers, temperate, and faithful in all things.
verses.1TI 3:12: Let servants be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.
verses.1TI 3:13: For those who have served well gain for themselves a good standing and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
verses.1TI 3:14: These things I write to you, hoping to come to you shortly,
verses.1TI 3:15: but if I wait long, that you may know how men ought to behave themselves in God’s house, which is the assembly of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

verses.1TI 4:14: Don’t neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the elders.
verses.1TI 4:15: Be diligent in these things. Give yourself wholly to them, that your progress may be revealed to all.

verses.2CO 11:1: I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you do bear with me.
verses.2CO 11:2: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you in marriage to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
verses.2CO 11:3: But I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness, so your minds might be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.
verses.2CO 11:4: For if he who comes preaches another Jesus whom we didn’t preach, or if you receive a different spirit which you didn’t receive, or a different “good news” which you didn’t accept, you put up with that well enough.
verses.2CO 11:5: For I reckon that I am not at all behind the very best apostles.
verses.2CO 11:6: But though I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not unskilled in knowledge. No, in every way we have been revealed to you in all things.
verses.2CO 11:7: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Good News free of charge?
verses.2CO 11:8: I robbed other assemblies, taking wages from them that I might serve you.
verses.2CO 11:9: When I was present with you and was in need, I wasn’t a burden on anyone, for the brothers, when they came from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my need. In everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and I will continue to do so.
verses.2CO 11:10: As the truth of Christ is in me, no one will stop me from this boasting in the regions of Achaia.
verses.2CO 11:11: Why? Because I don’t love you? God knows.
verses.2CO 11:18: Seeing that many boast after the flesh, I will also boast.
verses.2CO 11:21: To my shame, I speak as though we had been weak. Yet in whatever way anyone is bold (I speak in foolishness), I am bold also.
verses.2CO 11:22: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the offspring of Abraham? So am I.
verses.2CO 11:23: Are they servants of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself.) I am more so: in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, and in deaths often.
verses.2CO 11:24: Five times I received forty stripes minus one from the Jews.
verses.2CO 11:25: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. I have been a night and a day in the deep.
verses.2CO 11:26: I have been in travels often, perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils in the sea, perils among false brothers;
verses.2CO 11:27: in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness.
verses.2CO 11:28: Besides those things that are outside, there is that which presses on me daily: anxiety for all the assemblies.
verses.2CO 11:29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I don’t burn with indignation?
verses.2CO 11:30: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that concern my weakness.
verses.2CO 12:1: It is doubtless not profitable for me to boast, but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
verses.2CO 12:2: I know a man in Christ who was caught up into the third heaven fourteen years ago—whether in the body, I don’t know, or whether out of the body, I don’t know; God knows.
verses.2CO 12:3: I know such a man (whether in the body, or outside of the body, I don’t know; God knows),
verses.2CO 12:4: how he was caught up into Paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
verses.2CO 12:5: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in my weaknesses.
verses.2CO 12:6: For if I would desire to boast, I will not be foolish; for I will speak the truth. But I refrain, so that no man may think more of me than that which he sees in me or hears from me.
verses.2CO 12:7: By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively.
verses.2CO 12:8: Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
verses.2CO 12:9: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
verses.2CO 12:10: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.

verses.2CO 1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:
verses.2CO 1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2CO 1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,
verses.2CO 1:4: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
verses.2CO 1:5: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.
verses.2CO 1:6: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.
verses.2CO 1:7: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so you are also of the comfort.
verses.2CO 1:18: But as God is faithful, our word toward you was not “Yes and no.”
verses.2CO 1:19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me, Silvanus, and Timothy—was not “Yes and no,” but in him is “Yes.”
verses.2CO 1:20: For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.
verses.2CO 1:21: Now he who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,
verses.2CO 1:22: who also sealed us and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.
verses.2CO 3:1: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you?
verses.2CO 3:2: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men,

verses.2CO 3:4: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God,
verses.2CO 3:5: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God,
verses.2CO 3:6: who also made us sufficient as servants of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
verses.2CO 3:15: But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.

verses.2CO 3:17: Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
verses.2CO 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.

verses.2CO 4:6: seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

verses.2CO 3:8: won’t service of the Spirit be with much more glory?
verses.2CO 3:9: For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.
verses.2CO 3:10: For most certainly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.
verses.2CO 3:11: For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.

verses.2CO 4:9: pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;

verses.2CO 4:11: For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
verses.2CO 4:12: So then death works in us, but life in you.
verses.2CO 5:14: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.
verses.2CO 5:15: He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.
verses.2CO 5:16: Therefore we know no one according to the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.
verses.2CO 5:17: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
verses.2CO 5:18: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
verses.2CO 5:19: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
verses.2CO 5:20: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
verses.2CO 5:21: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

verses.2CO 6:10: as sorrowful yet always rejoicing, as poor yet making many rich, as having nothing and yet possessing all things.
verses.2CO 8:1: Moreover, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the assemblies of Macedonia,

verses.2CO 8:3: For according to their power, I testify, yes and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,

verses.2CO 8:6: So we urged Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace.
verses.2CO 8:7: But as you abound in everything—in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in your love to us—see that you also abound in this grace.
verses.2CO 8:8: I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of your love.
verses.2CO 8:9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.

verses.2KI 11:1: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.

verses.2KI 11:3: He was with her hidden in the LORD’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.2KI 11:4: In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the captains over hundreds of the Carites and of the guard, and brought them to him into the LORD’s house; and he made a covenant with them, and made a covenant with them in the LORD’s house, and showed them the king’s son.
verses.2KI 11:9: The captains over hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and they each took his men, those who were to come in on the Sabbath with those who were to go out on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.2KI 11:10: The priest delivered to the captains over hundreds the spears and shields that had been King David’s, which were in the LORD’s house.
verses.2KI 11:11: The guard stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, along by the altar and the house, around the king.
verses.2KI 11:12: Then he brought out the king’s son, and put the crown on him, and gave him the covenant; and they made him king and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, “Long live the king!”
verses.2KI 11:13: When Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she came to the people into the LORD’s house;
verses.2KI 11:14: and she looked, and behold, the king stood by the pillar, as the tradition was, with the captains and the trumpets by the king; and all the people of the land rejoiced, and blew trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Treason! Treason!”
verses.2KI 11:15: Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds who were set over the army, and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks. Kill anyone who follows her with the sword.” For the priest said, “Don’t let her be slain in the LORD’s house.”
verses.2KI 11:16: So they seized her; and she went by the way of the horses’ entry to the king’s house, and she was slain there.
verses.2KI 11:17: Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be the LORD’s people; also between the king and the people.

verses.2KI 11:20: So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. They had slain Athaliah with the sword at the king’s house.

verses.2KI 22:12: The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Achbor the son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying,
verses.2KI 22:13: “Go inquire of the LORD for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found; for great is the LORD’s wrath that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not listened to the words of this book, to do according to all that which is written concerning us.”
verses.2KI 23:1: The king sent, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.
verses.2KI 23:2: The king went up to the LORD’s house, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him—with the priests, the prophets, and all the people, both small and great; and he read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the LORD’s house.
verses.2KI 23:3: The king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD to walk after the LORD and to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes with all his heart and all his soul, to confirm the words of this covenant that were written in this book; and all the people agreed to the covenant.
verses.2KI 24:8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother’s name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
verses.2KI 24:9: He did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, according to all that his father had done.
verses.2KI 24:10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
verses.2KI 24:11: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it,
verses.2KI 24:12: and Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon—he, his mother, his servants, his princes, and his officers; and the king of Babylon captured him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.2KI 24:13: He carried out from there all the treasures of the LORD’s house and the treasures of the king’s house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the LORD’s temple, as the LORD had said.
verses.2KI 24:14: He carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valor, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. No one remained except the poorest people of the land.
verses.2KI 24:15: He carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, with the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his officers, and the chief men of the land. He carried them into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.2KI 24:16: All the men of might, even seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths one thousand, all of them strong and fit for war, even them the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon.
verses.2KI 24:17: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s father’s brother, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
verses.2KI 25:1: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it; and they built forts against it around it.
verses.2KI 25:2: So the city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.2KI 25:3: On the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine was severe in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.2KI 25:4: Then a breach was made in the city, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden (now the Chaldeans were against the city around it); and the king went by the way of the Arabah.
verses.2KI 25:5: But the Chaldean army pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
verses.2KI 25:6: Then they captured the king and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they passed judgment on him.
verses.2KI 25:7: They killed Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
verses.2KI 25:8: Now in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.2KI 25:9: He burned the LORD’s house, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. He burned every great house with fire.
verses.2KI 25:10: All the army of the Chaldeans, who were with the captain of the guard, broke down the walls around Jerusalem.
verses.2KI 25:11: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive the rest of the people who were left in the city and those who had deserted to the king of Babylon—all the rest of the multitude.
verses.2KI 25:12: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to work the vineyards and fields.
verses.2KI 2:1: When the LORD was about to take Elijah up by a whirlwind into heaven, Elijah went with Elisha from Gilgal.
verses.2KI 2:6: Elijah said to him, “Please wait here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” He said, “As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” Then they both went on.
verses.2KI 2:7: Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance; and they both stood by the Jordan.
verses.2KI 2:8: Elijah took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the waters; and they were divided here and there, so that they both went over on dry ground.
verses.2KI 2:9: When they had gone over, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you, before I am taken from you.” Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me.”
verses.2KI 2:10: He said, “You have asked a hard thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so.”
verses.2KI 2:11: As they continued on and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
verses.2KI 2:12: Elisha saw it, and he cried, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” He saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces.
verses.2KI 2:13: He also took up Elijah’s mantle that fell from him, and went back and stood by the bank of the Jordan.

verses.2KI 4:10: Please, let’s make a little room on the roof. Let’s set a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp stand for him there. When he comes to us, he can stay there.”
verses.2KI 4:11: One day he came there, and he went to the room and lay there.
verses.2KI 4:14: He said, “What then is to be done for her?” Gehazi answered, “Most certainly she has no son, and her husband is old.”
verses.2KI 4:15: He said, “Call her.” When he had called her, she stood in the door.

verses.2KI 5:1: Now Naaman, captain of the army of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honorable, because by him the LORD had given victory to Syria; he was also a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.
verses.2KI 5:2: The Syrians had gone out in bands, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little girl, and she waited on Naaman’s wife.
verses.2KI 5:3: She said to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”
verses.2KI 5:4: Someone went in and told his lord, saying, “The girl who is from the land of Israel said this.”
verses.2KI 5:5: The king of Syria said, “Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” He departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothing.
verses.2KI 5:6: He brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, “Now when this letter has come to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, that you may heal him of his leprosy.”
verses.2KI 5:7: When the king of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to heal a man of his leprosy? But please consider and see how he seeks a quarrel against me.”
verses.2KI 5:8: It was so, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
verses.2KI 5:9: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariots, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
verses.2KI 5:10: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall come again to you, and you shall be clean.”
verses.2KI 5:11: But Naaman was angry, and went away and said, “Behold, I thought, ‘He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place, and heal the leper.’
verses.2KI 5:12: Aren’t Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Couldn’t I wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in a rage.
verses.2KI 5:13: His servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”
verses.2KI 5:14: Then went he down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
verses.2KI 5:15: He returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him; and he said, “See now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel. Now therefore, please take a gift from your servant.”
verses.2KI 5:16: But he said, “As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will receive none.” He urged him to take it; but he refused.
verses.2KI 5:17: Naaman said, “If not, then, please let two mules’ load of earth be given to your servant; for your servant will from now on offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods, but to the LORD.

verses.2SA 11:1: At the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.
verses.2SA 11:2: At evening, David arose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof, he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful to look at.
verses.2SA 11:3: David sent and inquired after the woman. One said, “Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, Uriah the Hittite’s wife?”
verses.2SA 11:4: David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned to her house.
verses.2SA 11:5: The woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, “I am with child.”
verses.2SA 11:6: David sent to Joab, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.2SA 11:7: When Uriah had come to him, David asked him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.
verses.2SA 11:8: David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.
verses.2SA 11:9: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and didn’t go down to his house.
verses.2SA 11:10: When they had told David, saying, “Uriah didn’t go down to his house,” David said to Uriah, “Haven’t you come from a journey? Why didn’t you go down to your house?”
verses.2SA 11:13: When David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk. At evening, he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but didn’t go down to his house.
verses.2SA 11:14: In the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.2SA 11:15: He wrote in the letter, saying, “Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck and die.”
verses.2SA 11:16: When Joab kept watch on the city, he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew that valiant men were.
verses.2SA 11:17: The men of the city went out and fought with Joab. Some of the people fell, even of David’s servants; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
verses.2SA 12:1: The LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city: the one rich, and the other poor.
verses.2SA 12:2: The rich man had very many flocks and herds,
verses.2SA 12:3: but the poor man had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him and with his children. It ate of his own food, drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.
verses.2SA 12:4: A traveler came to the rich man, and he didn’t want to take of his own flock and of his own herd to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
verses.2SA 12:5: David’s anger burned hot against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As the LORD lives, the man who has done this deserves to die!

verses.2SA 12:10: Now therefore the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised me and have taken Uriah the Hittite’s wife to be your wife.’
verses.2SA 12:11: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
verses.2SA 12:12: For you did this secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.’”
verses.2SA 12:13: David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.” Nathan said to David, “The LORD also has put away your sin. You will not die.
verses.2SA 12:14: However, because by this deed you have given great occasion to the LORD’s enemies to blaspheme, the child also who is born to you will surely die.”

verses.2SA 16:7: Shimei said when he cursed, “Be gone, be gone, you man of blood, and wicked fellow!
verses.2SA 16:8: The LORD has returned on you all the blood of Saul’s house, in whose place you have reigned! The LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son! Behold, you are caught by your own mischief, because you are a man of blood!”

verses.2SA 16:10: The king said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Because he curses, and because the LORD has said to him, ‘Curse David,’ who then shall say, ‘Why have you done so?’”

verses.2SA 1:11: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them; and all the men who were with him did likewise.

verses.2SA 24:10: David’s heart struck him after he had counted the people. David said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in that which I have done. But now, the LORD, put away, I beg you, the iniquity of your servant; for I have done very foolishly.”

verses.2SA 5:1: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and spoke, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.

verses.2SA 7:8: Now therefore tell my servant David this: ‘The LORD of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people, over Israel.

verses.2SA 7:24: You established for yourself your people Israel to be your people forever; and you, LORD, became their God.

verses.2TH 1:1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.2TH 1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2TH 1:3: We are bound to always give thanks to God for you, brothers, even as it is appropriate, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each and every one of you toward one another abounds,
verses.2TH 1:4: so that we ourselves boast about you in the assemblies of God for your perseverance and faith in all your persecutions and in the afflictions which you endure.
verses.2TH 1:5: This is an obvious sign of the righteous judgment of God, to the end that you may be counted worthy of God’s Kingdom, for which you also suffer.
verses.2TH 1:11: To this end we also pray always for you that our God may count you worthy of your calling, and fulfill every desire of goodness and work of faith with power,
verses.2TH 1:12: that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2TH 2:1: Now, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, we ask you
verses.2TH 2:2: not to be quickly shaken in your mind or troubled, either by spirit or by word or by letter as if from us, saying that the day of Christ has already come.
verses.2TH 2:3: Let no one deceive you in any way. For it will not be unless the rebellion comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of destruction.
verses.2TH 2:14: to which he called you through our Good News, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2TH 2:15: So then, brothers, stand firm and hold the traditions which you were taught by us, whether by word or by letter.
verses.2TH 2:16: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
verses.2TH 2:17: comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.
verses.2TH 3:1: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified, even as also with you,
verses.2TH 3:2: and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil men; for not all have faith.
verses.2TH 3:3: But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
verses.2TH 3:4: We have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do the things we command.
verses.2TH 3:5: May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and into the perseverance of Christ.
verses.2TH 3:6: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks in rebellion and not after the tradition which they received from us.
verses.2TH 3:7: For you know how you ought to imitate us. For we didn’t behave ourselves rebelliously among you,
verses.2TH 3:8: neither did we eat bread from anyone’s hand without paying for it, but in labor and travail worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you.
verses.2TH 3:9: This was not because we don’t have the right, but to make ourselves an example to you, that you should imitate us.
verses.2TH 3:10: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.”
verses.2TH 3:16: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
verses.2TH 3:17: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand, which is the sign in every letter. This is how I write.
verses.2TH 3:18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
verses.2TH 3:11: For we hear of some who walk among you in rebellion, who don’t work at all, but are busybodies.
verses.2TH 3:12: Now those who are that way, we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ, that they work with quietness and eat their own bread.

verses.2TI 1:2: to Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

verses.2TI 1:11: For this I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.

verses.2TI 1:13: Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.

verses.2TI 2:1: You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.

verses.2TI 3:17: that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
verses.2TI 4:1: I command you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at his appearing and his Kingdom:
verses.2TI 4:2: preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort with all patience and teaching.
verses.2TI 4:3: For the time will come when they will not listen to the sound doctrine, but having itching ears, will heap up for themselves teachers after their own lusts,
verses.2TI 4:4: and will turn away their ears from the truth, and turn away to fables.
verses.2TI 4:5: But you be sober in all things, suffer hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and fulfill your ministry.
verses.2TI 4:6: For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure has come.
verses.2TI 4:7: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
verses.2TI 4:8: From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give to me on that day; and not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing.
verses.2TI 4:16: At my first defense, no one came to help me, but all left me. May it not be held against them.
verses.2TI 4:17: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, that through me the message might be fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear. So I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
verses.2TI 4:18: And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work and will preserve me for his heavenly Kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.2TI 4:15: Beware of him, for he greatly opposed our words.
