verses.LUK 14:31: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
verses.LUK 14:32: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.
verses.LUK 14:33: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
verses.LUK 15:1: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
verses.LUK 15:2: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
verses.LUK 15:4: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
verses.LUK 15:5: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.LUK 15:6: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
verses.LUK 15:7: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
verses.LUK 15:8: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
verses.LUK 15:9: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’
verses.LUK 15:10: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
verses.LUK 15:11: He said, “A certain man had two sons.
verses.LUK 15:12: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.
verses.LUK 15:13: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
verses.LUK 15:14: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
verses.LUK 15:15: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
verses.LUK 15:16: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
verses.LUK 15:17: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
verses.LUK 15:18: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
verses.LUK 15:19: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
verses.LUK 15:20: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
verses.LUK 15:21: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
verses.LUK 15:22: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
verses.LUK 15:23: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
verses.LUK 15:24: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.
verses.LUK 15:25: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.LUK 15:26: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.
verses.LUK 15:27: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
verses.LUK 15:28: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.
verses.LUK 15:29: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
verses.LUK 15:30: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
verses.LUK 15:31: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
verses.LUK 15:32: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”
verses.LUK 16:1: He also said to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
verses.LUK 16:2: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
verses.LUK 16:3: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.
verses.LUK 16:4: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’
verses.LUK 16:5: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
verses.LUK 16:6: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
verses.LUK 16:7: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
verses.LUK 16:8: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
verses.LUK 16:9: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
verses.LUK 16:10: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
verses.LUK 16:11: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
verses.LUK 16:12: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
verses.LUK 16:13: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
verses.LUK 16:19: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
verses.LUK 16:20: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,
verses.LUK 16:21: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.LUK 16:22: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
verses.LUK 16:23: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
verses.LUK 16:24: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’
verses.LUK 16:25: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted and you are in anguish.
verses.LUK 16:26: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’
verses.LUK 16:27: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house—
verses.LUK 16:28: for I have five brothers—that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’
verses.LUK 16:29: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’
verses.LUK 16:30: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
verses.LUK 16:31: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”
verses.LUK 16:14: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.
verses.LUK 16:15: He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
verses.LUK 17:1: He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
verses.LUK 17:2: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.LUK 17:3: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
verses.LUK 17:4: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
verses.LUK 17:5: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
verses.LUK 17:6: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
verses.LUK 17:11: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
verses.LUK 17:12: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
verses.LUK 17:13: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
verses.LUK 17:14: When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
verses.LUK 17:15: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
verses.LUK 17:16: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
verses.LUK 17:17: Jesus answered, “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
verses.LUK 17:18: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner?”
verses.LUK 17:19: Then he said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
verses.LUK 17:20: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
verses.LUK 17:21: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
verses.LUK 17:22: He said to the disciples, “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
verses.LUK 17:23: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away or follow after them,
verses.LUK 17:24: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of one part under the sky, shines to another part under the sky, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
verses.LUK 17:25: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
verses.LUK 17:26: As it was in the days of Noah, even so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
verses.LUK 17:27: They ate, they drank, they married, and they were given in marriage until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
verses.LUK 17:28: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
verses.LUK 17:29: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky and destroyed them all.
verses.LUK 17:30: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
verses.LUK 17:31: In that day, he who will be on the housetop and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
verses.LUK 17:33: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
verses.LUK 17:34: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. One will be taken and the other will be left.
verses.LUK 17:35: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other will be left.”
verses.LUK 17:37: They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?” He said to them, “Where the body is, there the vultures will also be gathered together.”
verses.LUK 17:7: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table’?
verses.LUK 17:8: Wouldn’t he rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
verses.LUK 17:9: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
verses.LUK 17:10: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
verses.LUK 18:1: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up,
verses.LUK 18:2: saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God and didn’t respect man.
verses.LUK 18:3: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
verses.LUK 18:4: He wouldn’t for a while; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect man,
verses.LUK 18:5: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
verses.LUK 18:6: The Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
verses.LUK 18:7: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
verses.LUK 18:8: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
verses.LUK 18:35: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
verses.LUK 18:36: Hearing a multitude going by, he asked what this meant.
verses.LUK 18:37: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
verses.LUK 18:38: He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.LUK 18:39: Those who led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
verses.LUK 18:40: Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. When he had come near, he asked him,
verses.LUK 18:41: “What do you want me to do?” He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”
verses.LUK 18:42: Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”
verses.LUK 18:43: Immediately he received his sight and followed him, glorifying God. All the people, when they saw it, praised God.
verses.LUK 18:9: He also spoke this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others:
verses.LUK 18:10: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
verses.LUK 18:11: The Pharisee stood and prayed by himself like this: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of men: extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
verses.LUK 18:12: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’
verses.LUK 18:13: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
verses.LUK 18:14: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
verses.LUK 19:1: He entered and was passing through Jericho.
verses.LUK 19:2: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
verses.LUK 19:3: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.
verses.LUK 19:4: He ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.
verses.LUK 19:5: When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
verses.LUK 19:6: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.
verses.LUK 19:7: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”
verses.LUK 19:8: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
verses.LUK 19:9: Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
verses.LUK 19:10: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
verses.LUK 19:11: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.
verses.LUK 19:12: He said therefore, “A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.
verses.LUK 19:13: He called ten servants of his and gave them ten mina coins, and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’
verses.LUK 19:14: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’
verses.LUK 19:15: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.
verses.LUK 19:16: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’
verses.LUK 19:17: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
verses.LUK 19:18: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
verses.LUK 19:19: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’
verses.LUK 19:20: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,
verses.LUK 19:21: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’
verses.LUK 19:22: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down and reaping that which I didn’t sow.
verses.LUK 19:23: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
verses.LUK 19:24: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him and give it to him who has the ten minas.’
verses.LUK 19:25: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
verses.LUK 19:26: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.
verses.LUK 19:27: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”
verses.LUK 19:28: Having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
verses.LUK 19:29: When he came near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
verses.LUK 19:30: saying, “Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man has ever sat upon. Untie it and bring it.
verses.LUK 19:31: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”
verses.LUK 19:32: Those who were sent went away and found things just as he had told them.
verses.LUK 19:33: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
verses.LUK 19:35: Then they brought it to Jesus. They threw their cloaks on the colt and sat Jesus on them.
verses.LUK 19:36: As he went, they spread their cloaks on the road.
verses.LUK 19:37: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,
verses.LUK 19:38: saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
verses.LUK 19:39: Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”
verses.LUK 19:40: He answered them, “I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
verses.LUK 2:14: “Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
verses.LUK 19:41: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,
verses.LUK 19:42: saying, “If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.
verses.LUK 19:43: For the days will come on you when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,
verses.LUK 19:44: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”
verses.LUK 19:45: He entered into the temple and began to drive out those who bought and sold in it,
verses.LUK 19:46: saying to them, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”
verses.LUK 19:47: He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests, the scribes, and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.
verses.LUK 19:48: They couldn’t find what they might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he said.
verses.LUK 1:1: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,
verses.LUK 1:2: even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us,
verses.LUK 1:3: it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus;
verses.LUK 1:4: that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.

verses.LUK 4:15: He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.

verses.LUK 4:17: The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He opened the book, and found the place where it was written,
verses.LUK 4:20: He closed the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.
verses.LUK 4:21: He began to tell them, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
verses.LUK 1:26: Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
verses.LUK 1:27: to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
verses.LUK 1:29: But when she saw him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be.
verses.LUK 1:30: The angel said to her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
verses.LUK 1:31: Behold, you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and shall name him ‘Jesus.’
verses.LUK 1:32: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
verses.LUK 1:33: and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.”
verses.LUK 1:34: Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?”
verses.LUK 1:35: The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God.
verses.LUK 1:36: Behold, Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her who was called barren.
verses.LUK 1:37: For nothing spoken by God is impossible.”
verses.LUK 1:38: Mary said, “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
verses.LUK 1:39: Mary arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
verses.LUK 1:40: and entered into the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth.
verses.LUK 1:41: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
verses.LUK 1:42: She called out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
verses.LUK 1:43: Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
verses.LUK 1:44: For behold, when the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the baby leaped in my womb for joy!
verses.LUK 1:46: Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord.
verses.LUK 1:47: My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
verses.LUK 1:48: for he has looked at the humble state of his servant. For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed.
verses.LUK 1:49: For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
verses.LUK 1:50: His mercy is for generations and generations on those who fear him.
verses.LUK 1:51: He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
verses.LUK 1:52: He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly.
verses.LUK 1:53: He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty.
verses.LUK 1:54: He has given help to Israel, his servant, that he might remember mercy,
verses.LUK 1:55: as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
verses.LUK 1:56: Mary stayed with her about three months, and then returned to her house.
verses.LUK 1:5: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
verses.LUK 1:6: They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
verses.LUK 1:7: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well advanced in years.
verses.LUK 1:8: Now while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his division
verses.LUK 1:9: according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
verses.LUK 1:10: The whole multitude of the people were praying outside at the hour of incense.
verses.LUK 1:11: An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
verses.LUK 1:12: Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.

verses.LUK 24:38: He said to them, “Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?

verses.LUK 24:40: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
verses.LUK 24:41: While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
verses.LUK 24:42: They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.
verses.LUK 24:43: He took them, and ate in front of them.
verses.LUK 24:44: He said to them, “This is what I told you while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning me must be fulfilled.”
verses.LUK 24:45: Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.
verses.LUK 24:47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
verses.LUK 24:48: You are witnesses of these things.
verses.LUK 24:49: Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”
verses.LUK 24:50: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
verses.LUK 24:51: While he blessed them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
verses.LUK 24:52: They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.LUK 24:53: and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
verses.LUK 2:1: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.
verses.LUK 2:2: This was the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
verses.LUK 2:3: All went to enroll themselves, everyone to his own city.
verses.LUK 2:4: Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
verses.LUK 2:5: to enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.
verses.LUK 2:6: While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
verses.LUK 2:7: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
verses.LUK 2:8: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
verses.LUK 2:9: Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
verses.LUK 2:10: The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
verses.LUK 2:11: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
verses.LUK 2:12: This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
verses.LUK 2:13: Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God and saying,
verses.LUK 2:15: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
verses.LUK 2:16: They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
verses.LUK 2:17: When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
verses.LUK 2:18: All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.
verses.LUK 2:20: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
verses.LUK 2:21: When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

verses.LUK 2:23: (as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”),

verses.LUK 2:27: He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents brought in the child, Jesus, that they might do concerning him according to the custom of the law,

verses.LUK 2:34: Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary, his mother, “Behold, this child is appointed for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which is spoken against.
verses.LUK 2:35: Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
verses.LUK 2:36: There was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
verses.LUK 2:37: and she had been a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.
verses.LUK 2:38: Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
verses.LUK 2:41: His parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
verses.LUK 2:42: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;
verses.LUK 2:43: and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t know it,
verses.LUK 2:44: but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey; and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
verses.LUK 2:45: When they didn’t find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.
verses.LUK 2:46: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
verses.LUK 2:47: All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
verses.LUK 2:48: When they saw him, they were astonished; and his mother said to him, “Son, why have you treated us this way? Behold, your father and I were anxiously looking for you.”
verses.LUK 2:49: He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
verses.LUK 2:50: They didn’t understand the saying which he spoke to them.
verses.LUK 2:51: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.

verses.LUK 3:1: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
verses.LUK 3:2: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.
verses.LUK 3:3: He came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for remission of sins.
verses.LUK 3:4: As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.
verses.LUK 3:5: Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.
verses.LUK 3:6: All flesh will see God’s salvation.’”
verses.LUK 3:10: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?”
verses.LUK 3:11: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
verses.LUK 3:12: Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what must we do?”
verses.LUK 3:13: He said to them, “Collect no more than that which is appointed to you.”
verses.LUK 3:14: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
verses.LUK 3:15: As the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,
verses.LUK 3:16: John answered them all, “I indeed baptize you with water, but he comes who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.LUK 3:17: His winnowing fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
verses.LUK 3:18: Then with many other exhortations he preached good news to the people,
verses.LUK 3:21: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also had been baptized and was praying. The sky was opened,
verses.LUK 3:22: and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him; and a voice came out of the sky, saying “You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased.”
verses.LUK 4:1: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
verses.LUK 4:2: for forty days, being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days. Afterward, when they were completed, he was hungry.
verses.LUK 4:3: The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”
verses.LUK 4:4: Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
verses.LUK 4:5: The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
verses.LUK 4:6: The devil said to him, “I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I want.
verses.LUK 4:7: If you therefore will worship before me, it will all be yours.”
verses.LUK 4:8: Jesus answered him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”
verses.LUK 4:9: He led him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here,
verses.LUK 4:10: for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’
verses.LUK 4:11: and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.’”
verses.LUK 4:12: Jesus answering, said to him, “It has been said, ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’”
verses.LUK 4:13: When the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him until another time.
verses.LUK 4:22: All testified about him and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth; and they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
verses.LUK 4:23: He said to them, “Doubtless you will tell me this proverb, ‘Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in your hometown.’”
verses.LUK 4:24: He said, “Most certainly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
verses.LUK 4:25: But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land.
verses.LUK 4:26: Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
verses.LUK 4:27: There were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed, except Naaman, the Syrian.”
verses.LUK 4:28: They were all filled with wrath in the synagogue as they heard these things.
verses.LUK 4:29: They rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill that their city was built on, that they might throw him off the cliff.
verses.LUK 4:30: But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way.
verses.LUK 4:31: He came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He was teaching them on the Sabbath day,
verses.LUK 4:32: and they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
verses.LUK 4:33: In the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon; and he cried out with a loud voice,
verses.LUK 4:34: saying, “Ah! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
verses.LUK 4:35: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!” When the demon had thrown him down in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no harm.
verses.LUK 4:36: Amazement came on all and they spoke together, one with another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
verses.LUK 4:37: News about him went out into every place of the surrounding region.
verses.LUK 4:38: He rose up from the synagogue and entered into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and they begged him to help her.
verses.LUK 4:39: He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately she rose up and served them.
verses.LUK 4:40: When the sun was setting, all those who had any sick with various diseases brought them to him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
verses.LUK 4:41: Demons also came out of many, crying out and saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” Rebuking them, he didn’t allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
verses.LUK 4:42: When it was day, he departed and went into an uninhabited place and the multitudes looked for him, and came to him, and held on to him, so that he wouldn’t go away from them.
verses.LUK 4:43: But he said to them, “I must preach the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I have been sent.”
verses.LUK 4:44: He was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
verses.LUK 5:1: Now while the multitude pressed on him and heard the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
verses.LUK 5:2: He saw two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.
verses.LUK 5:3: He entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. He sat down and taught the multitudes from the boat.
verses.LUK 5:4: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.”
verses.LUK 5:5: Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.”
verses.LUK 5:6: When they had done this, they caught a great multitude of fish, and their net was breaking.
verses.LUK 5:7: They beckoned to their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
verses.LUK 5:8: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.”
verses.LUK 5:9: For he was amazed, and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which they had caught;
verses.LUK 5:10: and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive.”
verses.LUK 5:11: When they had brought their boats to land, they left everything, and followed him.
verses.LUK 5:12: While he was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
verses.LUK 5:13: He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
verses.LUK 5:14: He commanded him to tell no one, “But go your way and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing according to what Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
verses.LUK 5:15: But the report concerning him spread much more, and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
verses.LUK 5:16: But he withdrew himself into the desert and prayed.
verses.LUK 5:17: On one of those days, he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by who had come out of every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was with him to heal them.
verses.LUK 5:18: Behold, men brought a paralyzed man on a cot, and they sought to bring him in to lay before Jesus.
verses.LUK 5:19: Not finding a way to bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop and let him down through the tiles with his cot into the middle before Jesus.
verses.LUK 5:20: Seeing their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
verses.LUK 5:21: The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?”
verses.LUK 5:22: But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, answered them, “Why are you reasoning so in your hearts?
verses.LUK 5:23: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk’?
verses.LUK 5:24: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” he said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, arise, take up your cot, and go to your house.”
verses.LUK 5:25: Immediately he rose up before them, and took up that which he was laying on, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
verses.LUK 5:26: Amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God. They were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
verses.LUK 5:27: After these things he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”
verses.LUK 5:28: He left everything, and rose up and followed him.
verses.LUK 5:29: Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
verses.LUK 5:30: Their scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
verses.LUK 5:31: Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
verses.LUK 5:32: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
verses.LUK 5:33: They said to him, “Why do John’s disciples often fast and pray, likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”
verses.LUK 5:34: He said to them, “Can you make the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?
verses.LUK 5:35: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.”
verses.LUK 5:36: He also told a parable to them. “No one puts a piece from a new garment on an old garment, or else he will tear the new, and also the piece from the new will not match the old.
verses.LUK 5:37: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled and the skins will be destroyed.
verses.LUK 5:38: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.
verses.LUK 5:39: No man having drunk old wine immediately desires new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
verses.LUK 6:1: Now on the second Sabbath after the first, he was going through the grain fields. His disciples plucked the heads of grain and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
verses.LUK 6:2: But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why do you do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath day?”
verses.LUK 6:3: Jesus, answering them, said, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,
verses.LUK 6:4: how he entered into God’s house, and took and ate the show bread, and gave also to those who were with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”
verses.LUK 6:5: He said to them, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
verses.LUK 6:12: In these days, he went out to the mountain to pray, and he continued all night in prayer to God.
verses.LUK 6:13: When it was day, he called his disciples, and from them he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles:
verses.LUK 6:14: Simon, whom he also named Peter; Andrew, his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
verses.LUK 6:15: Matthew; Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus; Simon who was called the Zealot;
verses.LUK 6:16: Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who also became a traitor.
verses.LUK 6:17: He came down with them and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases,
verses.LUK 6:18: as well as those who were troubled by unclean spirits; and they were being healed.
verses.LUK 6:19: All the multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all.
verses.LUK 6:20: He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for God’s Kingdom is yours.
verses.LUK 6:21: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
verses.LUK 6:22: Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude and mock you, and throw out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
verses.LUK 6:23: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same thing to the prophets.
verses.LUK 6:24: “But woe to you who are rich! For you have received your consolation.
verses.LUK 6:25: Woe to you, you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
verses.LUK 6:26: Woe, when men speak well of you, for their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
verses.LUK 6:27: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
verses.LUK 6:28: bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
verses.LUK 6:29: To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your coat also.
verses.LUK 6:30: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.
verses.LUK 6:31: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
verses.LUK 6:32: “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
verses.LUK 6:33: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
verses.LUK 6:34: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.
verses.LUK 6:35: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
verses.LUK 6:36: “Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.
verses.LUK 6:37: Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.
verses.LUK 6:38: “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you.”
verses.LUK 6:39: He spoke a parable to them. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?
verses.LUK 6:40: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained will be like his teacher.
verses.LUK 6:41: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
verses.LUK 6:42: Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
verses.LUK 6:43: “For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.
verses.LUK 6:44: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
verses.LUK 6:45: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
verses.LUK 6:46: “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
verses.LUK 6:47: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show you who he is like.
verses.LUK 6:48: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
verses.LUK 6:49: But he who hears and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.”
verses.LUK 6:6: It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
verses.LUK 6:7: The scribes and the Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find an accusation against him.
verses.LUK 6:8: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise up and stand in the middle.” He arose and stood.
verses.LUK 6:9: Then Jesus said to them, “I will ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
verses.LUK 6:10: He looked around at them all, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.
verses.LUK 6:11: But they were filled with rage, and talked with one another about what they might do to Jesus.
verses.LUK 7:1: After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
verses.LUK 7:2: A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.
verses.LUK 7:3: When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.
verses.LUK 7:4: When they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him,
verses.LUK 7:5: for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”
verses.LUK 7:6: Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.
verses.LUK 7:7: Therefore I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed.
verses.LUK 7:8: For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
verses.LUK 7:9: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned and said to the multitude who followed him, “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.”
verses.LUK 7:10: Those who were sent, returning to the house, found that the servant who had been sick was well.
verses.LUK 7:11: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.
verses.LUK 7:12: Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, one who was dead was carried out, the only born son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.
verses.LUK 7:13: When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
verses.LUK 7:14: He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
verses.LUK 7:15: He who was dead sat up and began to speak. Then he gave him to his mother.
verses.LUK 7:16: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
verses.LUK 7:17: This report went out concerning him in the whole of Judea and in all the surrounding region.
verses.LUK 7:19: John, calling to himself two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for another?”
verses.LUK 7:20: When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?’”
verses.LUK 7:21: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.
verses.LUK 7:22: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
verses.LUK 7:23: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
verses.LUK 7:24: When John’s messengers had departed, he began to tell the multitudes about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
verses.LUK 7:25: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed and live delicately are in kings’ courts.
verses.LUK 7:26: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
verses.LUK 7:27: This is he of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
verses.LUK 7:28: “For I tell you, among those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
verses.LUK 7:29: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be just, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
verses.LUK 7:30: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him themselves.
verses.LUK 7:31: “To what then should I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
verses.LUK 7:32: They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
verses.LUK 7:33: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
verses.LUK 7:34: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
verses.LUK 7:35: Wisdom is justified by all her children.”
verses.LUK 7:36: One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house and sat at the table.
verses.LUK 7:37: Behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.
verses.LUK 7:38: Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
verses.LUK 7:39: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he said to himself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”
verses.LUK 7:40: Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, say on.”
verses.LUK 7:41: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
verses.LUK 7:42: When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”
verses.LUK 7:43: Simon answered, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
verses.LUK 7:44: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.
verses.LUK 7:45: You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
verses.LUK 7:46: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
verses.LUK 7:47: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.”
verses.LUK 7:48: He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
verses.LUK 7:49: Those who sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
verses.LUK 7:50: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
verses.LUK 8:1: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
verses.LUK 8:2: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
verses.LUK 8:3: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others who served them from their possessions.
verses.LUK 8:15: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
verses.LUK 8:16: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.
verses.LUK 8:17: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.
verses.LUK 8:18: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
verses.LUK 8:19: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.
verses.LUK 8:20: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”
verses.LUK 8:21: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”
verses.LUK 8:4: When a great multitude came together and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable:
verses.LUK 8:5: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
verses.LUK 8:6: Some seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
verses.LUK 8:7: Some fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it.
verses.LUK 8:8: Some fell into the good ground and grew and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
verses.LUK 8:9: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
verses.LUK 8:10: He said, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest it is given in parables, that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
verses.LUK 8:11: “Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
verses.LUK 8:12: Those along the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
verses.LUK 8:13: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root. They believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
verses.LUK 8:14: What fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life; and they bring no fruit to maturity.
verses.LUK 9:1: He called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
verses.LUK 9:2: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
verses.LUK 9:3: He said to them, “Take nothing for your journey—no staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money. Don’t have two tunics each.
verses.LUK 9:4: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.
verses.LUK 9:5: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”
verses.LUK 9:6: They departed and went throughout the villages, preaching the Good News and healing everywhere.
verses.LUK 9:11: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.
verses.LUK 9:12: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms and lodge and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”
verses.LUK 9:13: But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”
verses.LUK 9:14: For they were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
verses.LUK 9:15: They did so, and made them all sit down.
verses.LUK 9:16: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.
verses.LUK 9:17: They ate and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
verses.LUK 9:18: As he was praying alone, the disciples were near him, and he asked them, “Who do the multitudes say that I am?”
verses.LUK 9:19: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets has risen again.”
verses.LUK 9:20: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
verses.LUK 9:21: But he warned them and commanded them to tell this to no one,
verses.LUK 9:22: saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”
verses.LUK 9:23: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
verses.LUK 9:24: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake will save it.
verses.LUK 9:25: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
verses.LUK 9:26: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.
verses.LUK 9:28: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
verses.LUK 9:29: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
verses.LUK 9:30: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
verses.LUK 9:31: who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
verses.LUK 9:32: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.
verses.LUK 9:33: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.
verses.LUK 9:34: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.
verses.LUK 9:35: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
verses.LUK 9:36: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.
verses.LUK 9:43: They were all astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marveling at all the things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,
verses.LUK 9:44: “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man will be delivered up into the hands of men.”
verses.LUK 9:45: But they didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
verses.LUK 9:46: An argument arose among them about which of them was the greatest.
verses.LUK 9:47: Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a little child, and set him by his side,
verses.LUK 9:48: and said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For whoever is least among you all, this one will be great.”
verses.LUK 9:49: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow with us.”
verses.LUK 9:50: Jesus said to him, “Don’t forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us.”
verses.LUK 9:51: It came to pass, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem
verses.LUK 9:52: and sent messengers before his face. They went and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.
verses.LUK 9:53: They didn’t receive him, because he was traveling with his face set toward Jerusalem.
verses.LUK 9:54: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”
verses.LUK 9:55: But he turned and rebuked them, “You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.
verses.LUK 9:56: For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.” They went to another village.
verses.LUK 9:57: As they went on the way, a certain man said to him, “I want to follow you wherever you go, Lord.”
verses.LUK 9:58: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”
verses.LUK 9:59: He said to another, “Follow me!” But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
verses.LUK 9:60: But Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
verses.LUK 9:61: Another also said, “I want to follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say good-bye to those who are at my house.”
verses.LUK 9:62: But Jesus said to him, “No one, having put his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.”
verses.LUK 9:7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,
verses.LUK 9:8: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
verses.LUK 9:9: Herod said, “I beheaded John, but who is this about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.
verses.LEV 13:1: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
verses.LEV 13:2: “When a man shall have a swelling in his body’s skin, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his body the plague of leprosy, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
verses.LEV 13:44: he is a leprous man. He is unclean. The priest shall surely pronounce him unclean. His plague is on his head.
verses.LEV 13:45: “The leper in whom the plague is shall wear torn clothes, and the hair of his head shall hang loose. He shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’
verses.LEV 13:46: All the days in which the plague is in him he shall be unclean. He is unclean. He shall dwell alone. His dwelling shall be outside of the camp.
verses.LEV 19:1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.LEV 19:2: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
verses.LEV 19:11: “‘You shall not steal. “‘You shall not lie. “‘You shall not deceive one another.
verses.LEV 19:12: “‘You shall not swear by my name falsely, and profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
verses.LEV 19:13: “‘You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob him. “‘The wages of a hired servant shall not remain with you all night until the morning.
verses.LEV 19:14: “‘You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
verses.LEV 19:15: “‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor show favoritism to the great; but you shall judge your neighbor in righteousness.
verses.LEV 19:16: “‘You shall not go around as a slanderer among your people. “‘You shall not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
verses.LEV 19:17: “‘You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
verses.LEV 19:18: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
verses.LEV 23:1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.LEV 23:4: “‘These are the set feasts of the LORD, even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed season.
verses.LEV 23:5: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, is the LORD’s Passover.
verses.LEV 23:6: On the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread to the LORD. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.LEV 23:7: In the first day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.
verses.LEV 23:8: But you shall offer an offering made by fire to the LORD seven days. In the seventh day is a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.’”
verses.LEV 23:9: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.LEV 23:10: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When you have come into the land which I give to you, and shall reap its harvest, then you shall bring the sheaf of the first fruits of your harvest to the priest.
verses.LEV 23:11: He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, to be accepted for you. On the next day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
verses.LEV 23:15: “‘You shall count from the next day after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering: seven Sabbaths shall be completed.
verses.LEV 23:16: The next day after the seventh Sabbath you shall count fifty days; and you shall offer a new meal offering to the LORD.
verses.LEV 23:27: “However on the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement. It shall be a holy convocation to you. You shall afflict yourselves and you shall offer an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.LEV 23:34: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the feast of booths for seven days to the LORD.
verses.LEV 23:35: On the first day shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.
verses.LEV 23:36: Seven days you shall offer an offering made by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day shall be a holy convocation to you. You shall offer an offering made by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you shall do no regular work.
verses.LEV 23:37: “‘These are the appointed feasts of the LORD which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to offer an offering made by fire to the LORD, a burnt offering, a meal offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, each on its own day—
verses.LEV 23:38: in addition to the Sabbaths of the LORD, and in addition to your gifts, and in addition to all your vows, and in addition to all your free will offerings, which you give to the LORD.
verses.LEV 25:1: The LORD said to Moses on Mount Sinai,
verses.LEV 25:8: “‘You shall count off seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years; and there shall be to you the days of seven Sabbaths of years, even forty-nine years.
verses.LEV 25:9: Then you shall sound the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land.
verses.LEV 25:10: You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee to you; and each of you shall return to his own property, and each of you shall return to his family.
verses.LEV 25:11: That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee to you. In it you shall not sow, neither reap that which grows of itself, nor gather from the undressed vines.
verses.LEV 25:12: For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat of its increase out of the field.
verses.LEV 25:13: “‘In this Year of Jubilee each of you shall return to his property.
verses.LEV 25:14: “‘If you sell anything to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
verses.LEV 25:15: According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor. According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you.
verses.LEV 25:16: According to the length of the years you shall increase its price, and according to the shortness of the years you shall diminish its price; for he is selling the number of the crops to you.
verses.LEV 25:17: You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.
verses.MAL 1:14: “But the deceiver is cursed who has in his flock a male, and vows and sacrifices to the Lord a defective thing; for I am a great King,” says the LORD of Armies, “and my name is awesome among the nations.”
verses.MAL 2:1: “Now, you priests, this commandment is for you.
verses.MAL 2:2: If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart, to give glory to my name,” says the LORD of Armies, “then I will send the curse on you, and I will curse your blessings. Indeed, I have cursed them already, because you do not take it to heart.
verses.MAL 2:8: But you have turned away from the path. You have caused many to stumble in the law. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.MAL 2:9: “Therefore I have also made you contemptible and wicked before all the people, according to the way you have not kept my ways, but have had respect for persons in the law.
verses.MAL 2:10: Don’t we all have one father? Hasn’t one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
verses.MAL 3:1: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me! The Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple. Behold, the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, is coming!” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.MAL 3:2: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderers’ soap;
verses.MAL 3:3: and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver; and they shall offer to the LORD offerings in righteousness.
verses.MAL 3:4: Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant to the LORD as in the days of old and as in ancient years.
verses.MAL 4:5: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
verses.MAL 4:6: He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the earth with a curse.”
verses.MAL 3:13: “Your words have been harsh against me,” says the LORD. “Yet you say, ‘What have we spoken against you?’
verses.MAL 3:14: You have said, ‘It is vain to serve God,’ and ‘What profit is it that we have followed his instructions and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of Armies?
verses.MAL 3:15: Now we call the proud happy; yes, those who work wickedness are built up; yes, they tempt God, and escape.’
verses.MAL 3:16: Then those who feared the LORD spoke one with another; and the LORD listened and heard, and a book of memory was written before him for those who feared the LORD and who honored his name.
verses.MAL 3:17: They shall be mine,” says the LORD of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make. I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
verses.MAL 3:18: Then you shall return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him who serves God and him who doesn’t serve him.
verses.MAL 4:1: “For behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace, when all the proud and all who work wickedness will be stubble. The day that comes will burn them up,” says the LORD of Armies, “so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
verses.MAL 4:2: But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves of the stall.
verses.MIC 2:1: Woe to those who devise iniquity and work evil on their beds! When the morning is light, they practice it, because it is in the power of their hand.
verses.MIC 2:2: They covet fields and seize them, and houses, then take them away. They oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.
verses.MIC 2:3: Therefore the LORD says: “Behold, I am planning against these people a disaster, from which you will not remove your necks, neither will you walk haughtily, for it is an evil time.
verses.MIC 2:4: In that day they will take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, saying, ‘We are utterly ruined! My people’s possession is divided up. Indeed he takes it from me and assigns our fields to traitors!’”
verses.MIC 2:5: Therefore you will have no one who divides the land by lot in the LORD’s assembly.
verses.MIC 5:2: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will come out to me who is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings out are from of old, from ancient times.
verses.MIC 5:3: Therefore he will abandon them until the time that she who is in labor gives birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the children of Israel.
